source.title: MuPT: A Generative Symbolic Music Pretrained Transformer
source.authors: Xing-Wei Qu; Yuelin Bai; Yi Ma; Zi-Ya Zhou; Ka-Man Lo; Jia-Heng Liu; Ruibin Yuan; Le-Jun Min; Xueling Liu; Tian-Yu Zhang; Xin-Run Du; Shuyue Guo; Yi-Ming Liang; Yizhi Li; Shangda Wu; Jun-Ting Zhou; Tian-Yu Zheng; Ziyang Ma; F. Han; Wei Xue; Gus G. Xia; Emmanouil Benetos; Xiang Yue; Cheng-Hua Lin; Xu Tan; Stephen W. Huang; Wen-Hu Chen; Jie Fu; Ge Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling-law behavior in autoregressive symbolic music models, a different modality and data regime from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study measures validation-loss fits across model sizes, token counts, data repetition settings and scaling-law variants, and reports results for larger runs. Scaling-law results cited from other papers are background only, not rows. Music-generation and human-evaluation results do not test the listed scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: Fits Chinchilla, Data-Constrained and modified laws to validation loss of 190M–1.07B symbolic-music (ABC) decoder models under data repetition. It then checks extrapolation to 1.97B and 4.23B runs (the 'test' columns of Tables 3/7). This is a new modality with results on power-law form, extrapolation and fit-dependence.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find Chinchilla fits moderate cases but fails for small data early in training and under repetition-driven overfitting. Their SMS Law (Chinchilla plus an N·D term and a GELU overfitting term) fits and extrapolates best to 1.97B/4.23B runs, and they recommend it for scaling symbolic-music models under limited data. Their main paper contributions are the MuPT models and SMT-ABC notation.
record.recipe_differences: Studies decoder-only symbolic-music models and validation-loss scaling. Its SMS Law modifies existing scaling formulas to handle limited unique data, model-size effects and overfitting; it is not a reproduction of the original language-model studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Fit choice changes the reported test performance; results also depend on whether curves after early-stop points are included. The study reports that the Chinchilla error direction differs for small versus large models paired with limited data, and that overfitting occurs beyond 3 epochs in the stated 1.07B run.
record.problems: The paper gives no uncertainty intervals for the scaling-law fit metrics. The compute-allocation comparison is reported for one compute budget, and multiple curve comparisons appear as figures without pointwise numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-law rows omitted. Pointwise loss values from Figures 3, 5, 6 and 7 were not extracted because they are shown graphically without numerical values; the text-described trends are recorded in r21-r22 and r24. Unrelated music-generation and human-evaluation outcomes are outside the claim versions.

untested.parts: Study is symbolic music, not text language-model pretraining. Its rows belong under V5.
Only one compute budget (1.2e21 FLOPs). No optimal N or D exponents across budgets, and the Chinchilla-optimal alternative was not trained.
No shape ablation; model shapes co-vary with size (Table 1).
Downstream metrics (repetition rate, intra-similarity, human preference) are not related to scale or loss.
Extrapolation span is only ~2–4x in parameters (1.07B to 1.97B/4.23B), not orders of magnitude.
Only symbolic music; no image, video, fine-tuning or transfer settings.

missing.what: Training-set fits: Chinchilla R2 0.9347, Huber 0.0109 (Table 3) and R2 0.9443 (Table 7). The plain law fits in-sample but fails to extrapolate; authors say Chinchilla fits 'moderate' cases well.
Activation-function ablation for the overfitting term: sigmoid R2 0.6030 vs ~0.978 for others. Fit quality depends on this choice.
Compute-optimal predictions at 1.2e21 FLOPs: SMS gives 2.10B/1.98B at 2.82 epochs (loss 0.5279/0.5280); Chinchilla gives 990M at 6.1 epochs.
4.23B run said to confirm the SMS overfitting prediction; no number given.

record.verdict_notes: The 'test' set is the larger 1.97B and 4.23B runs, so test metrics measure extrapolation. SMS Law and Eq 2/Eq 11 are the authors' own laws; their superiority is the study's method claim, but it bears on V7 and V2. Table 6's 'test' GELU values equal Table 3's SMS train values, possibly mislabelled. No uncertainty is reported, and the test set is only two models.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test loss as a function of compute independently with the other quantities non-bottleneck, or establish the stated behavior across several orders of magnitude in general language models.
Tests extrapolation in this symbolic-music setup, not language-model runs generally.
Reports an allocation comparison at one stated compute budget; does not test whether both optimal parameter count and token count follow stable powers across multiple compute budgets.
Tests symbolic music, not image, video, fine-tuning or transfer regimes.
Does not test language-model parameter-counting choices or the cited Kaplan–Hoffmann setup differences.

rows.subject: 1.97B-parameter MuPT model
rows.operation_detail: Train under the stated compute budget and compare its validation loss with the SMS Law and Chinchilla allocation predictions
rows.measure: Validation loss
rows.baseline: SMS Law estimate 0.5280 for a 1.98B-parameter model over 2.82 epochs
rows.note: The text describes the measured loss as a minimal increase relative to the SMS Law estimate. The stated model size and training duration differ from that estimate.
rows.check: Not V3: one compute budget, no allocation exponent. Measured 0.529 for 1.97B at ~2.5 epochs vs SMS prediction 0.5280 for 1.98B at 2.82 epochs; configurations differ slightly. Chinchilla's recommended 990M/6.1-epoch run was not trained, so the allocation comparison is untested by measurement. Drop V1/V5.

source_check.correct: Observed agreement with a nearby SMS configuration and observed allocation dependence for V7; orders-of-magnitude power-law extrapolation in V2 cannot be determined.
source_check.problem: The numerical comparison is correct, but it does not establish V2's stated extrapolation range.

rows.subject: 1.07B-parameter MuPT model
rows.operation_detail: Continue training and observe validation-loss behavior with repeated data
rows.measure: Validation loss and overfitting behavior
rows.note: The paper presents this as validation of the SMS Law's advantage under the tested data constraint; no numerical loss is given.
rows.check: Overfitting beyond 3 epochs is a bend away from a monotone power law (observed for V7) and cuts against Chinchilla's 6.1-epoch suggestion. No number given. Drop V1/V2/V3.

source_check.correct: Observed bending/non-monotonicity for V7; a qualification of monotone power-law behavior for V5, rather than observed preservation of that form.
source_check.problem: Observed overfitting supports V7 but cannot be assigned the same effect state for V5.
